On Wed, May 15, 2013 at 4:09 PM, Peter Li <li.pe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Why would the starting value need to be changed? 
 
The init values don't need to be changed.
 

As for changing the sampler and the number of iterations, couldn't we just implement a new method that would add "--[insert sampler call here]" to the method that actually starts the sampling?

That sounds good and should work. Want to start working on that?
 

Perhaps, we could do this by adding a new string variable in model_test_fixture called 'sampler' which would be added in the get_command method inside model_test_fixture. We could assign the sampler name or whatever the call for it is to the new string and have NUTS be the default if nothing is specified.

Yes, definitely. If you think of a way to make model_test_fixture more flexible, go ahead and do it. It was only designed with one sampler in mind and I think we've now outgrown its original intent. Did you want to work on that for a short amount of time? Or do you want to work together on it?

 
I believe we could do something similar for number of iterations. And for iterations, how would we determine the number of iterations necessary?

Trial and error.

 

On 5/15/13 3:41 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
Hi Peter,

Testing framework:
- hasn't been sorted out yet.
- do you want to help specify the behavior of what the framework should do? Since you're adding another use-case for the testing framework, I think it's time we rethink the whole thing. Maybe even pull it out of google test. I'm not sure. Here is a small list of requirements I was thinking about when I built it:
  * cross platform
  * configurable for each model
  * each model may have its own:
     - # iterations
     - values to check
     - values to skip
     - data and init files
     - special code for dealing with unidentified models
   * have the results integrate into Jenkins -- we've used junit output for the time being, but we could look for another solution.
- that all ran the default sampler, but now you're considering adding a different sampler, so we'd have to consider a few more things. I guess we want to keep everything but the first value, but allow changes to # iterations and the sampler parameters. Is there anything else we should really consider?
 
If you want to play with the sampler testing framework, let's start discussing what needs to be in and then we can build up something that's going to be reusable and flexible enough.


Daniel

messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Metropolis testing (and generalizing testing for other
parts:
I've been thinking some more about the testing framework. The way I set up the new framework, all of the model tests are run for all samplers, but I'm not sure that's what we want. Will there be models that we do not want to test against certain samplers just because it would take so long?

If so, a different set-up for the framework would be to have separate test files for each sampler. (i.e. for bugs_examples/vol/blocker, we could have blocker_nuts_test.cpp, blocer_unit_metro_test.cpp, etc.). Then, if we do not want to test a certain sampler we just don't include that file. But if we do it this way, I think it would end up compiling the model as many times as we want to test it, which would significantly increase the amount of time it takes to run test-models. That's one of the main reasons why I opted to setup the tests the other way. However, another plus for this is that we can create make commands (if that's what they're called) that will test all the models against certain samplers in case we don't want to run all of the models against all the samplers (NUTS, unit/diag/dense metro and later RM-HMC, Ensemble (with a few variations)).

We could also opt to keep the current setup and just have an if/else statement inside the model_test_fixture that doesn't run the tests if the number of iterations is greater than 500k or whatever upper bound we choose. As for being able to just test certain samplers, that would not be difficult, but I don't see a way to just give a command that does that--we'd have to go into model_test_fixture and comment out the tests that call the other samplers. This still wouldn't be difficult, but it just wouldn't be systematic.



Peter

parts:
You bring up a good point about what we want to test.

Ideally, we would test everything --- every sampler in
every configuration on every model. I think of this as more of a functional
or regression test than a unit test, though. And we know ahead
of time that not every model is going to be fittable with every
sampler under every configuration, so it's a bit of a tricky
business configuring it all.

What I'd really like to see is something that looks more like
unit tests for the models. Tests that exercise all of the functions
being generated by the model rather than how they run as a whole.

Then, we can back off and run the functional/regression tests
much less frequently than every pull request.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Metropolis testing (and generalizing testing for other
parts:
On Thursday, May 23, 2013 2:53:22 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
What I'd really like to see is something that looks more like
unit tests for the models.  Tests that exercise all of the functions
being generated by the model rather than how they run as a whole.

I do think we need a test-grad metatarget that just compiles all the models, runs them with --test-grad, and returns 0 iff lp__ is finite and the AD gradient is close to the numerical gradient. But that is more of a unit test of the libstan and stanc than a test of a particular sample. To test a sampler, I think we need something like

-- Generate a random correlation matrix
-- Maybe scale with random standard deviations to get a covariance matrix
-- Generate lots of multivariate normal data with mean zero and that covariance matrix
-- Run a sampler
-- Verify that posterior is not too far from the population parameters

You could play around with how the population gets generated, but in general, we need a set of tests with known populations to supplement all the toy BUGS models.

Ben
